posts.title: Active asset allocator SIFs in September — the smallest group, the sharpest asymmetry
posts.summary: An allocator long-short fund is meant to dial market exposure up and down with the cycle. In September, one did it brilliantly — qsif's allocator captured 77% of the market's upside but only 6% of its downside — while two others ran the quieter, steadier version of the same mandate. Part three of a per-category series.
posts.author: SIFintel Research

posts.title: Equity long-short SIFs in September — where "hedged" meant very different things
posts.summary: An equity long-short fund should rise with the market and fall a lot less. In September the category cushioned the drop as a group — but the hedge quality ranged from genuinely asymmetric to funds that simply owned the market. Part two of a per-category series.
posts.author: SIFintel Research

posts.title: Hybrid long-short SIFs in September — the category that is supposed to be boring
posts.summary: A hybrid long-short fund has one job — don't lose big. Measured that way, September was a quiet success for most: the median hybrid absorbed just 11% of the NIFTY's fall at 3.4% volatility. But two "hybrids" behaved like equity funds, and one behaved like a hedge fund. Part one of a per-category series.
posts.author: SIFintel Research

posts.title: September's 6% drop was the real mandate test — and some "hedged" SIFs failed it
posts.summary: The NIFTY fell 6.1% in September and the midcaps 7.9%. Almost every SIF "beat" the index — but that is the floor, not the achievement. Judged on what each strategy is built to do (low downside capture, not relative return), the hybrids and allocators largely earned their keep, while a handful of "hybrid" and "long-short" schemes revealed far more market risk than their label implies.
posts.author: SIFintel Research

posts.title: Two legs, one quarter — the ten SIFs that were up in both
posts.summary: The market gave managers a clean natural experiment this quarter: a 5.85% rally into early August, then a 3.47% fall. Of the 21 SIF schemes with NAVs covering both legs, ten finished each of them in the black.
posts.author: SIFintel Research

posts.title: The NIFTY fell 3.5% in a month. Every long-short SIF fell less.
posts.summary: Between 3 August and 2 September 2026 the NIFTY 50 lost 3.47%. Across the 30 Indian SIF schemes with a full month of published NAVs, not one lost that much — and 18 of them finished the month higher. Includes the full month-by-month return record for every scheme against the NIFTY.
posts.author: SIFintel Research
